interpretations.rationale: Current account: a recovery driven by a replica that does not itself hold the instance's command replaces the value carried by its prepare replies with a NOOP, and the replacement can be executed to a completed contradiction of a value another live replica has committed. Three executed witnesses bound the trigger. (1) Receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment): the accepted value X at ballot 0 is replaced; the self reply's fabricated VBallot 8 shadows the genuine reply at value ballot 0; sub-case 6 selects startPhase1 with state.NOOP(); the holder loses X (comparison 1 violated, witness 20). (2) Receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 (successor experiment d9390caf51ee413aaf05a733db9b99ff-experiment): the owner commits X (index 6) and its Commit reaches only replica 2 (index 10), so a live replica holds X COMMITTED (index 11); the recoverer's prepare reply reports X with Status COMMITTED at value ballot 0 (index 16); the recovery still emits the NOOP (index 19); the first attempt stalls (index 21); the executor's retry dispatches (index 24) and commits the NOOP at replicas 3 and 4 (indices 25, 27) while replica 2 keeps X (index 26) - two live replicas hold different decided values for instance (0,0) (comparison 0 violated, witness 25). (3) Receipt 893f6180a4514a8d9e20a1d5e6698542 (fixed experiment 6fbba03eb3354cf384e0044c37ac7542-experiment) shows the same replacement with the instance owner alive throughout: replica 0 keeps its command X in its own instance (index 2) and its own prepare reply carries it (index 3), yet replica 3, which holds no command for the instance, proposes the NOOP (indices 6, 7) and the recovered decision is installed on the live owner as a COMMITTED NOOP (indices 9 and 12), with the pending client request re-offered on a new instance (index 10) and later completed (index 17). So the defect does not require the instance owner to fail: a live but stalled owner whose instance is recovered by a replica lacking the command loses the command, and the client's request survives only because the re-propose path re-offers it. Mechanism: startRecoveryForInstance sets lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal and then overwrites inst.vbal with the freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145, 1150-1153), so the self reply's VBallot outranks the genuine reply at value ballot 0 and the adoption loop (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246) leaves lb.cmds nil and lb.status NONE; the accepted attributes are dropped with it. Recorded knowledge used: aa497fcd14934325ba2eabe45fefecd1-knowledge-0/-1 (fabricated self reply; ballot-gated adoption), cbbf11dd38d843f1b6acf52fd5b6e82e-knowledge-0 (status guard on the restarted phase), 602b7dcab8064d2ab9113ac315a40743-knowledge-0 (re-propose protection), summarised in the Fact ed76b573b9fe4bde9565d4b4678cda85-knowledge-0.
counterevidence: The defect is bounded to coordinators that lack the command, and that bound is executed: control experiment 242eaa8afa384a87b0952fbcd4b074b4-experiment (receipt 9d07449105684a498113db891da025d9) replayed the value-adoption crash pattern with the recovery driven by replica 2, which holds X; its preservation comparisons hold, evaluating indices 17 and 19-20.

Event 16 of receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 shows the adoption is a ballot ordering, not a general discard: a reply whose value ballot exceeded the coordinator's own recovery ballot would still be adopted.

The committed peer keeps its value in its own state, and the protection is the absence of a writer rather than a guard: handleCommit returns immediately when inst.Status >= COMMITTED (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082), and handlePreAccept changes nothing for such an instance because its only mutation for Status >= ACCEPTED sits behind the guard inst.Cmds == nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:807-813), which is false for a replica that holds the committed command. The contradiction is therefore between two replicas' decided values rather than a silent rewrite at the holder.

The live owner's request is not silently dropped: handleCommit re-offers its pending proposal on a new instance (receipt 893f6180a4514a8d9e20a1d5e6698542 indices 10 and 17), so the client's completion is delayed rather than lost - but the originally accepted command and its ordering are gone.

The countervailing ballot-climb path in makeBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451) is gated on IsLeader, which is false in all these executions and in epaxos.New; the master-designated leader's behaviour is treated in the separate recovery-authority question.
limitations: One configuration and one instance in all three receipts: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), one PUT command (key 1) and the NOOP the recovery generates.

The harness schedules delivery explicitly: the startRecoveryForInstance calls are the functions the executor invokes after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417), but no run() loop or executeCommands goroutine was active, and the crash points were chosen by the harness within the target's permitted failure model.

The completed contradiction required the executor's retry to be invoked a second time by the harness; the contradiction itself was measured, but the executor's own retry cadence was modelled rather than run.

Reaching the recovering replica in the executed scenarios required a peer of the instance to fail so that the accept broadcast skipped it (the target's own Alive mechanism); a deployment where the accepting peers and the pre-accepting peers coincide for every replica was not shown to reach the same state.
Incidental observation not used by the claim: the recovered committed instance carries Seq -1 at replicas 2, 3 and 4 while startPhase1 computed seq 0.
